metadata.note: The Laurinburg and Southern Railroad (chartered 1909 by Laurinburg mill and merchant interests; John F. McNair president, James A. Jones general manager) built 18 mi Johns (ACL connection) - Laurinburg (SAL connection) - Wagram, opening to freight in July 1909 and to passengers 11 June 1910, and bought the 12-mi Wagram - Raeford line from the Aberdeen and Rockfish on 12 Nov 1921. Passenger traffic (a mixed train) was discontinued by NC Corporation Commission order in 1923-24; the company then ran a Laurinburg - Raeford highway bus (franchise listed July 1928). Freight continues to this day as the LRS. Drawn: Johns - Wagram 1910-1923 only. One company throughout; no Rule 4 split.
sources: NC Corporation Commission annual/biennial reports (archive.org: annualreportofco1910nort ... annualreportofco1916nort, reportofcorporat1918nort ... reportofcorporat1924nort), Laurinburg and Southern returns: Johns - Wagram 18 mi, passenger-train revenue in every return FY1911 - CY1923; 1923-24 biennium 'Application for discontinuance of passenger traffic. Granted.'
Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue, Laurinburg and Southern entry ('Operated for freight service only') and station index

metadata.omitted: Wagram - Raeford (12 mi, ex-Aberdeen and Rockfish, owned by the L&S from 12 Nov 1921) is NOT drawn: the only evidence of L&S passenger trains on it is road-wide revenue that roughly doubled after the purchase, which does not show which stations were served. Omitted rather than invented (research/branches/laurinburg_and_southern_railroad.txt block [2], drawable: NONE). The Aberdeen and Rockfish layer does not draw it either.
not_yet_sourced: Whether L&S passenger (mixed) trains ever ran Wagram - Raeford, 1921-1924. Settles whether Wagram - Raeford can be drawn.

The Hoke County Journal (Raeford) of 19 June 1924, p.5, said by a search-engine summary to print an L&S schedule 'effective December 9, 1923' with daily trains Johns - Laurinburg - Wagram - Raeford (also hits 6 Dec 1923 p.1 and 17 Jan 1924 p.1). UNREAD - newspapers.digitalnc.org refused connections. If it is real and current in June 1924, Johns - Wagram extends to 1924 and Wagram - Raeford gains its first confirmed year(s).
Exact date of the passenger discontinuance: the NCCC 1923-24 order is undated. The drawn end is the last confirmed year (1923), not a known end.

What the 1924-1931 'passenger' revenue and revenue-passenger counts in the NCCC returns were: a highway bus that replaced the trains (bus franchise by July 1928; 1930-31 line headed 'passenger train service and Highway Bus') or unadvertised mixed-train / caboose riding. Not drawn under omit-rather-than-invent.
The nature of the 1910 'through service with the Atlantic Coast Line' (NCpedia): through cars or only a connection at Johns.
Any timetable for any year: headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.
metadata.freight_only_audit: Built 2026-11-05 to Rule 1: nothing drawn after 1923. Not drawn: the whole road after the 1923-24 passenger discontinuance (freight only; 'Operated for freight service only' in the Feb 1952 Guide - 1951 is NOT an end year), the Laurinburg - Raeford highway bus (a motor coach), the 'L Line' and industrial sidings at Laurinburg, and the L&S holding company's later freight short lines.

properties.speed_source: estimated: 18-mile steam short line worked by a mixed train; no timetable running time has been seen for 1910-1923. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py (Operator subclassed to also match operator/name = 'Laurinburg and Southern Railroad'). The line survives in OSM as the LRS: live track (railway=rail) Johns - Laurinburg - north of Laurinburg and embargoed track (railway=disused) on to Wagram, tagged old_railway_operator='Laurinburg and Southern', operator/name='Laurinburg and Southern Railroad' (ways 169448670, 1258939412, 1107669931, 1107669945-1107669968, 1119068231-1119068242, 1258942346, 16768337, 1029357092, 1029357091, 1119068244, 1119068246). Way 169448670 at the Johns end carries old_railway_operator='ACL' but operator/name 'Laurinburg and Southern Railroad'. The trace ran 17.0 mi on L&S-tagged ways and 0 mi on any other operator (no CSX ex-ACL or ex-SAL track). The 'Laurinburg and Southern Railroad (L Line)' ways (operator tag only, an eastward spur at Laurinburg) were deliberately excluded. Spellings 'L&S' and 'LRS' in old_railway_operator return nothing in OSM. OSM abandoned/rail-trail ways and OpenHistoricalMap were queried for 34.65,-79.50,34.92,-79.33: OHM has no railway ways there. Waypoints (Nominatim, each type checked): Johns (hamlet, Scotland County; 0.6 km from the drawn south end, which is the L&S's own south end at the ACL/CSX main), Laurinburg (town; 0.5 km), Wagram (town; 0.1 km). Simplified with Douglas-Peucker 8 m, trim_reversals; no spurs.
properties.geometry_quality: Johns - Wagram: traced 17.0 mi on the L&S's own surviving OSM track against a documented 18.00 mi (every NCCC return 1910-1919) - 5.6% short. Chainage at Laurinburg 5.9 mi vs c.6 (Fowler mileposts Johns 30 / Laurinburg 24 from Raeford). No approximated (straight-line) legs. The south end stops where the L&S track meets the ex-ACL (CSX South End Subdivision) main near Johns; the shortfall is probably the original Johns station/wye trackage and any later realignment, not a missing leg. ERA CAVEAT: the drawn alignment is the present-day (2020s OSM) LRS track, live to north of Laurinburg and disused beyond; it follows the 1909-10 right-of-way as far as is known, but any yard, siding or minor realignment in Laurinburg since 1923 has not been checked against a period map. The line north of Wagram to Raeford (ex-Aberdeen and Rockfish, L&S from 1921) is in OSM but is deliberately not drawn - see metadata.

segments.note: Passenger service began 11 June 1910 (NCpedia); the NC Corporation Commission returns bracket it (no passenger revenue line in the return to 30 June 1910, $2,017.99 passenger-train revenue in FY1911) and show passenger-train revenue every year through CY1923 ($1,875.02 in 1923, more than 1922 - a full or near-full year of service). The FY1912 return labels that revenue 'mixed', so the passenger service was a mixed train, with through service via the Atlantic Coast Line at Johns from later in 1910 (NCpedia; whether through cars or only a connection is not established). END: the Commission granted the road's 'application for discontinuance of passenger traffic' in its 1923-1924 biennium, entry undated - so the end bracket is 1923-1924. 1923 is the last CONFIRMED year; 1924 is withheld because the only evidence for it (a Hoke County Journal, Raeford, 19 June 1924 L&S schedule 'effective December 9, 1923', known only from a search-engine summary) has not been read. Do not extend without evidence. Passenger revenue after 1923 is not counted as rail: from at least July 1928 the company held a Laurinburg - Raeford highway-bus franchise, and its 1930-31 return heads the line 'passenger train service and Highway Bus'. Freight continued: 'Operated for freight service only' in the Feb 1952 Official Guide; the road is still the LRS freight short line (Gulf & Ohio since 1994). headway_min 1440 (one round trip a day) is an ESTIMATE - no timetable has been seen; the payrolls show one engine crew in most years, consistent with a single daily mixed train.
sources: Segment-level: start 11 June 1910 from NCpedia, corroborated by the NCCC returns (no passenger revenue to 30 June 1910, revenue FY1911 onward); end 1923 from the NCCC CY1923 return (passenger-train revenue) and the 1923-24 biennial report's order granting discontinuance of passenger traffic (undated). headway_min is an estimate, not sourced.
